sentences.text: The holotype of Nyasasaurus was collected in the 1930s from the Lifua Member of the Manda Formation in southern Tanzania by Francis Rex Parrington.
The remains were first described in 1956 in a doctoral thesis and referred to as Specimen 50b.

A new description was published in 2013 by Sterling Nesbitt, Paul Barrett, Sarah Werning, and Christian Sidor, which ensured the validity of the name Nyasasaurus and changed the specific name to parringtoni in honor of Parrington.
Analysis of the humerus indicates rapid bone growth with interwoven fibers, many blood vessel channels, and few lines of arrested growth.
Nyasasaurus is confidently classified within Archosauria and Dinosauriformes, and possibly within Dinosauria.
The humerus of Nyasasaurus does not share any unique traits exclusively with any other Triassic archosaur clade.
The parent group of Nyasasaurus is listed as Dinosauria.
If radiometric dating is correct, Nyasasaurus would be Carnian in age, significantly reducing the time gap between it and other early dinosaurs.
A 1986 hypothesis suggested Nyasasaurus was a primitive prosauropod dinosaur, but this was disputed.
Not all paleontologists accept the younger Carnian age proposed for the formation containing Nyasasaurus.
The SHRIMP dating methods used to determine the age of the Río Seco de la Quebrada Formation have been criticized as less accurate than CA-TIMS dating.
